title: Soft-priority tiling for low-tail-latency FlashAttention
body:
Goal

Reduce 99th/99.9th tail latency for short interactive requests when KV is partially paged to host and kernels contend for memory bandwidth. The specific scenario: many short chat-like requests (<= 64 tokens) with heavy cache churn where fused FlashAttention kernels block on paged-KV prefetch and large fused kernels, causing spikes in end-to-end latency.

Motivation and observations (from profiling)

- Workload: mixture of short latency-sensitive requests and occasional long-generation requests. Short requests dominate request-per-second but are sensitive to jitter.
- Profiling (prof-run-2025-01-08): tail spikes correlate with: (a) large fused-kernel launches that force allocator/eviction work, (b) aggressive prefetches for cold KV cohorts that saturate PCIe/NVLink for small intervals, (c) busy-warps blocked on atomic rendezvous for slab allocation.
- Existing heuristics (global prefetch when slot miss) are too blunt: they either prefetch too little (causing sync stalls) or prefetch too much (burst bandwidth).

Idea: Soft-priority tiling + cooperative warp backoff

High level: introduce a soft-priority tiling/scheduling layer inside the kernel launcher and within kernels that:
1) splits work units into small tiles optimized for low-latency short requests,
2) assigns a dynamic soft-priority score to tiles based on request SLO and current KV residency,
3) allows high-priority tiles to opportunistically preempt/steal micro-slices of execution resources from low-priority ones via cooperative backoff and warp-level yield,
4) throttles aggressive KV prefetches when hardware bandwidth budget is near exhaustion using a lightweight in-kernel governor.

Key components

- Tile granularity: micro-tiles of sequence-length x head-chunk (e.g., 16 tokens x 32 heads) that map to a warp-group. This size should be tunable per model/sequence distribution.

- Soft-priority score: function of {request_type_score, kv-residency-penalty, historical-latency-exceedance}. Score in [0,100]. Higher score wins micro-scheduling slots.

- Cooperative yield: implement a warp-level fast-path that checks a global per-SM arbitration flag at safe yield points (end of micro-tile processing). If a higher-priority tile appears, current warp withdraws to a light-weight spinback (N cycles) to allow scheduler/launcher to reassign. This is a cooperative scheme — no preemptive context switch.

- In-kernel bandwidth governor: track a lightweight token-bucket estimate of DMA/prefetch bytes per timeslice (per-GPU or per-NVLink domain). Prefetchers consult the bucket; if low, they fall back to on-demand one-shot prefetch instead of aggressive windowed fetch. Bucket refilled at tunable rate based on observed throughput.

Launcher-level heuristics

- Categorize incoming requests at enqueue time by SLO label: latency-critical vs background. This label derived from route metadata (console/route config) or inline hint from callers.
- Greedy packing: fill SM queues with a mix of micro-tiles prioritized by soft-score, ensuring that at least X% of SM slots are reserved for latency-critical tiles when load > threshold. X is a config param (default 30%).

Pseudo-code (launcher):

  enqueue(request R):
    tiles = split_into_microtiles(R)
    for tile in tiles: tile.score = compute_soft_score(R, tile)
    sort tiles by score desc
    push tiles to per-SM queues with round-robin placement, respecting reserved slots

In-kernel yield sketch:

  for microtile in assigned_tiles:
    process_microtile()
    if (warp_id == 0 && read_global_high_priority_flag()):
      write_back_partial_state()
      cooperative_backoff_spin(small_backoff)
      continue where left off on reclaimed scheduling pass

Design tradeoffs and risks

- Cooperative yield complexity: adds small overhead to normal path (few cycles per tile). Need microbenchmark to ensure overall throughput not regressed for heavy batched workloads.
- Starvation risk: background (low-priority) tiles may be slowed; mitigate via aging (score increases) and guaranteed-progress counters.
- Accuracy of bandwidth governor: token-bucket approximation may be noisy; start conservative and expose tuning.
- Kernel complexity and verification: new synchronization points and global flags may interact badly with existing streaming primitives (FlashAttention fast paths).

Experimentation plan

1) Microbenchmarks: synthetic mix of short (<=32 tokens) and long (>=512 tokens) requests; measure p50/p95/p99 before/after enabling soft-priority at multiple batching conditions.
2) Prefetch stress test: simulate cold-KV storms and measure PCIe/NVLink utilization and per-request latency jitter with and without governor.
3) Throughput regression: run sustained large-batch throughput tasks to confirm no >5% throughput regression.
4) A/B in staging: route 10% production-like traffic mixture with telemetry (trace spans, per-token latency) and compare.

Implementation notes and milestones

- Phase 0 (spike): implement launcher-side micro-tiling + soft-score sorting in CPU/host runtime; route small tiles to existing kernels (no in-kernel yield) to validate scheduling gains. (2 weeks)
- Phase 1: implement in-kernel cooperative yield and simple token-bucket governor; integrate with FlashAttention fused kernels as opt-in flag. (4-6 weeks)
- Phase 2: polish aging/guaranteed-progress, add per-SM telemetry counters, expose config through console. (3 weeks)

Open questions / TODOs

- What default tile sizes are optimal for our catalog of models? Need auto-profiling script.
- How to best express SLO/priority hints in API without encouraging misuse? (Route configs vs inline hints).
- Interaction with pinned/dedicated allocations in Redwood Dedicated: reserved capacity should have different governor parameters.
- Safety: how to fail closed if in-kernel arbitration deadlocks? Need watchdog and fallback to conservative mode.

Next steps

- Quick spike: host-side micro-tiling prototype by 2025-01-20 (owner: Asha).
- Follow-up design review with kernel owners and SRE on 2025-01-22. Add profiling harness for short-chat workload.

Notes to self

- Check prior experiments: "asynchronous-burst-coalescer-paged-kv-sketch.json" for burst control ideas.
- Bring this idea to kernel sync; ask Rajiv to add per-SM counters in the next runtime release.
